latest.title: Strong surface assay results from Whistlejacket
latest.content:
3 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8463O
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd
03 August 2026
3 August 2026
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd
("Bradda", "BHL" or the "Company")
Whistlejacket Surface Sampling Returns up to 4.24% Li₂O, Strengthening 2026 Drill Targets
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM: BHLL), the North America-focused lithium development company, is pleased to announce strong surface assay results from its Whistlejacket Lithium Project ("Whistlejacket" or "WJ"), held subject to the Company's Option to Joint Venture agreement with Kennecott Exploration Company ("KEX"). The results, as part of ongoing exploration work by the Company, include spodumene-bearing pegmatite outcrops identified for priority sampling in areas targeted by the Company's planned 2026 drilling programme. These new results coupled with KEX surface sample results will be used to further refine drill targeting ahead and alongside the commencement of drilling.
Highlights:
·
High-grade lithium assays of up to 4.24% Li₂O returned from the second phase of surface sampling at Whistlejacket;
·
Out of 190 rock samples analysed, 29 (15.3%) returned grades above 0.50% Li₂O, including 15 (7.9%) above 1.50% Li₂O;
·
These impressive results strengthen the prospectivity of several priority areas identified by KEX and provide additional geochemical support for refining the Company's 2026 drill targets;
·
Five prospective areas outside the current 2026 permitted drill programme have been highlighted for further evaluation, including one newly identified by the BHL exploration team, expanding the pipeline of potential targets for future drilling;
·
A further 43 surface rock samples are undergoing laboratory analysis, providing additional near-term results to support ongoing drill target generation and refinement;
·
All 190 rock samples returned iron content below 1.0% Fe, with the majority below 0.5% Fe, consistent with the low-iron characteristics observed across the sampled LCT type pegmatites;
·
Following the Company's recently announced successful fundraise, Bradda is well positioned to rapidly advance its 2026 exploration programmes at Whistlejacket and San Domingo, including the commencement of planned drilling activities (see PR dated July 17, 2026).
Ia
n Stalker, Executive Chair, commented:
"These results, including grades of up to 4.24% Li₂O, significantly inform and strengthen our confidence in the targets selected for the upcoming drilling programme at Whistlejacket, and endorse our overall excitement about the future of the project and its potential to become a significant asset for Bradda Head. Importantly, our ongoing exploration continues to identify additional prospective areas beyond our current permitted drill targets, expanding the potential exploration pipeline. Following our recent successful fundraise, we are well positioned to move quickly to advance our exploration programmes at both Whistlejacket and San Domingo. With further assays pending and core drilling on the horizon, we believe Whistlejacket is entering an exciting phase of value creation for Bradda Head."
Surface samples
The Company has received assay results from its second phase of surface sampling at Whistlejacket (Figure 1). Following the initial rock-chip sampling programme announced in our 15 June 2026 PR, sampling continued to focus on newly generated targets identified by the BHL exploration team and on areas previously explored by KEX, with the objective of increasing sampling density and refining targets ahead of drilling. To date, BHL has collected and received laboratory results on 250 samples, 190 of which are presented in this announcement.
A total of 198 samples were submitted to SGS for analysis, comprised of 190 rock samples and 8 quality control samples (CRM's, Figure 1). 29 of the rock chip samples returned lithium grades exceeding 0.50% Li₂O, including 24 samples grading above 1.00% Li₂O (representing 12.6% of all rock samples submitted, excluding CRM's) and 15 samples exceeding 1.50% Li₂O (Table 1), with the highest assay returning 4.24% Li₂O from a near-horizontal pegmatite in the vicinity of the main targets. The range of Li2O values is 4.24% to 0.04%. Some of the lower values appear to reside in spodumene bearing pegmatites, but display increased levels of altered spodumene, something not commonly found at Whistlejacket. All samples within this batch are select from rock chips from outcrops deemed to contain visible lithium bearing minerals, dominated by spodumene.
All 190 rock samples returned low iron contents (<1.0% Fe), with the majority containing less than 0.5% Fe, reinforcing the favorable mineralogical and metallurgical characteristics of the project.
In addition to lithium, the rock sampling programme returned elevated concentrations of tantalum (Ta), niobium (Nb), cesium (Cs) and rubidium (Rb), consistent with rare-element enrichment within the Whistlejacket pegmatite system. Maximum values included 304 ppm Ta, 270 ppm Nb, 208 ppm Cs and 5,659 ppm Rb, with 90 of the 190 rock samples returning more than 1,000 ppm Rb (Table 1). The distribution of these elements provides additional geochemical vectors that may assist in interpreting pegmatite fractionation and refining exploration targeting.
The results have also highlighted five prospective areas outside the current 2026 permitted drilling programme (Figure 2). Four correspond with areas previously identified through KEX exploration activities. Areas A and B were previously highlighted in Figure 2 of the Company's announcement dated 15 June 2026, while Areas C and D represent zones of sub-vertical pegmatites where increased sampling density has provided additional evidence of mineralized continuity (Figure 3). A fifth area (Area E) represents a newly generated target identified by the BHL exploration team and comprises a steeply dipping pegmatite displaying fresh crystalline spodumene mineralization. Preliminary field observations indicate a pegmatite body approximately 8 m wide at surface that appears to narrow towards its contact with the meta tuff. Collectively, these areas expand the Company's pipeline of prospective drill targets and will be further evaluated for potential inclusion in future exploration and drilling programmes.
A further 43 surface rock samples have been submitted for laboratory analysis, with results expected to provide additional geochemical coverage and support continued target refinement ahead of and alongside the 2026 exploration programme.
QAQC
Rock-chip samples were collected under the supervision of Hugo Zuniga, Senior Project Manager. Sample locations were recorded in the field, and samples were bagged, secured and transported to the Company's core facility before delivery by Company personnel to the SGS preparation facility in Tempe, Arizona. Following sample preparation, pulps were shipped to SGS Laboratories in Burnaby, British Columbia, Canada, for analysis using sodium peroxide fusion with ICP-AES and ICP-MS finish (method GE_ICM90A50). Certified reference materials were inserted into the sample stream as part of the Company's QA/QC procedures and reviewed by Hugo Zuniga. The Company Qualified Person (QP), Mr Joey Wilkins, consents to the inclusion of the technical information in this release and the context in which it appears.
Figure 1. Location of new Bradda Head surface samples (white), historical KEX sampling (cyan).
Figure 2. Location of new Bradda Head surface samples (white), historical KEX sampling (no labels), previously identified prospective areas (yellow boxes) and newly identified Bradda Head target area (purple box).
Figure 3.- New target opportunity areas identified from previous mapping and recent exploration results.
Table 1.- Assay table showing selected results with Li2O grades > 1.5 %. (Li2O values have been rounded to two decimal places).
Qualified Person (Bradda Head)
Joey Wilkins, B.Sc., P.Geo., is an external consultant and the Qualified Person who reviewed and approved the technical disclosures in this news release. Mr Wilkins is a graduate of the University of Arizona with a B.Sc. in Geology with more than 40 years of experience in mineral exploration and is a qualified person under the AIM Rules and a Qualified Person as defined under NI-43-101. Mr Wilkins consents to the inclusion of the technical information in this release and context in which it appears.

About Bradda Head Lithium Ltd.
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd. is a North America-focused lithium development group. The Company currently has interests in a variety of projects, the most advanced of which are in Central and Western Arizona: The Basin Project (Basin East Project and Basin West Project) and the San Domingo Project.
The Basin East Project has a Measured Mineral Resource of 20 Mt at an average grade of 929 ppm Li for a total of 99 kt LCE and an Indicated Mineral Resource of 122 Mt at an average grade of 860 ppm Li and an Inferred Mineral Resource of 499 Mt at an average grade of 810 ppm Li for a total of 2.81 Mt LCE (https://www.accesswire.com/883697/bradda-head-lithium-ltd-announces-updated-mineral-resource-expansion-basin-project). A plan of operation was approved by BLM in 2025 for the Basin West area. The Company is currently progressing the Environmental Assessment ("EA") process for the Basin West area.
The San Domingo Project comprises 248 claims covering approximately 1850 acres, located primarily on BLM land, along with two Arizona State Land Department claims. To date, 108 drill holes totaling 13,089 m of core drilling have been completed across three drilling campaigns. The project area hosts more than 1,000 mapped pegmatites, of which 18 have been identified as priority targets, with six tested by drilling. The area currently holds two active Notices of Intent (NOI) permits, and updated drilling plans are in place that can be implemented once all required permits for the pegmatite targets are secured. The objective of the next exploration phase is to further delineate the most prospective areas and advance them toward potential Mineral Resource Estimation (MRE) and NI 43-101 compliant reporting.
The Whistlejacket Project comprises nine Arizona State Land Department Mineral Exploration Permits (MEPs), covering a total of 2,010.7 hectares. The project is subject to a definitive Option to Joint Venture agreement with Kennecott Exploration Company (KEX) and targets spodumene-bearing pegmatites. KEX previous Exploration include 19 drilled diamond drill holes totaling 4,188 meters, with all holes intersecting lithium mineralization. Notable results include 51.0 meters at 1.11% Li₂O in hole WSTL0009 and 19.47 meters at 1.66% Li₂O in hole WSTL0008 (https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news-article/BHL/whistlejacket-review-of-previous-results/17534407). In addition, the project has benefited from extensive surface mapping, sampling, airborne geophysics, and the acquisition of high-resolution aerial imagery, significantly enhancing the geological understanding and overall value of the asset.
The Group intends to continue to develop its three phase one projects in Arizona, whilst endeavoring to unlock value at its other prospective pegmatite and brine assets in Arizona, Nevada, and Pennsylvania.

latest.content:

29 July 2026
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd
("Bradda", "BHL" or the "Company")
Drill Rig Secured for 2026 Whistlejacket Exploration Programme
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM: BHL), the North America-focused lithium development company, is pleased to announce that it has secured an Arizona licensed drilling contractor to commence the 2026 infill exploration drilling campaign at its Whistlejacket ("WJ") Project in Arizona.
Highlights:
•
The Drill rig is anticipated to mobilize by the end of July 2026 to WJ and immediately commence drilling;
•
Drill sites and any access routes will be prepared in advance of the rig arrival, however, BHL will also be utilizing drill sites previously prepared by Kennecott Exploration Co. ("KEX"), that had not been previously reclaimed;
•
Bradda Head plans to drill up to 20 diamond drill holes, totaling approximately 3,657.6 meters (12,000 ft);
•
All authorized expenditures from the drilling programme are applicable to the requirements of the Option Agreement with KEX;
•
Planned drill holes are designed to infill and expand known lithium mineralization identified by KEX in their 2023 drilling programme, specifically, offsetting holes WSTL-008, -009, and 006, which cut @ 0.97% Li2O over 10.74m, 1.31% Li2O over 13.56m, and 0.79% Li2O over 9.75m respectively (see PR 04/07/2026);
•
Several shallow core holes will also target pegmatites recently sampled by BHL that contain 3.03%, 2.04%, and 2.07% Li2O (See PR 06/15/2026 for surface sample details) or well mineralized outcrops previously sampled by KEX;
•
BHL has secured all drilling permits from the Arizona State Land Department ("ASLD");
•
The Phase 3 drilling programme has been specifically designed to support the preparation of the project's initial NI 43-101 technical report and, subject to continued exploration success, the delivery of a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") by the end of 2027;
•
Earthwork contractors have been secured and work is scheduled to commence next week, with equipment being mobilized to upgrade access roads and construct the drill pads required for the programme;
•
Following the Company's successful fundraise, Bradda is well positioned to advance its 2026 exploration programmes at Whistlejacket and San Domingo, including the commencement of planned drilling activities (see PR dated 17 July 2026 and 28 July 2026).
Ia
n Stalker, Executive Chair, commented:
"This is another major milestone for Bradda Head as we continue to advance Whistlejacket toward its maiden Mineral Resource Estimate. With permits in place, infrastructure preparations underway, and an experienced exploration team ready to mobilize, we are ready to commence drilling by the end of July. This programme is designed to improve our understanding of the scale and continuity of the mineralized system at Whistlejacket and represents another important step in unlocking the value of a highly prospective hard-rock lithium project in the United States. Following our recent successful fundraise, we are well positioned to move quickly and advance our exploration programmes at both Whistlejacket and San Domingo. "

Bradda Head Lithium Ltd
("Bradda", "BHL" or the "Company")
Result of WRAP Retail Offer
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM: BHLL), the North America-focused lithium development group, is pleased to confirm, further to the announcements made on 17 July 2026 and 21 July 2026, the result of its WRAP Retail Offer at the Issue Price of 2.25 pence per share. The Company announces that it has raised aggregate gross proceeds of approximately £131,562 pursuant to the WRAP Retail Offer, alongside the previously announced Fundraise. Accordingly, the Company will issue a total of 5,847,198 new Ordinary Shares at the Issue Price pursuant to the WRAP Retail Offer.
In addition, the Company received signed subscription letters from interested parties post the Fundraise announcement on 17 July 2026, raising gross proceeds of £30,000 and will issue 1,333,333 new Ordinary Shares at the Issue Price.

WRAP Retail Offer for up to £200,000
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM: BHLL), the North America-focused lithium development group, is pleased to announce a retail offer via the Winterflood Retail Access Platform ("
WRAP
") to raise up to £200,000 (the "
WRAP Retail Offer
") through the issue of new ordinary shares of no par value each in the capital of the Company ("
Ordinary Shares
"). Under the WRAP Retail Offer up to 8,888,888 new Ordinary Shares (the "
WRAP Retail Offer Shares
") will be made available at a price of 2.25 pence per share.
As part of the WRAP Retail Offer, the Company has agreed that 1 warrant for every 2 WRAP Retail Offer Shares will be granted (for no additional subscription cost), with each warrant entitling the holder to acquire one new Ordinary Share at a price of 5 pence for a period of 2 years from the date on which they are issued (the "
Warrants
"). The issue of the Warrants is subject the successful admission of the Warrants to settlement in uncertificated form through CREST. It is also anticipated that the Warrants will be eligible for CREST settlement approximately a month after Admission (defined below). The Warrants will not be admitted to trading on AIM or any other regulated market.
In addition to the WRAP Retail Offer and as announced on 17 July 2026 ("
Fundraise Announcement
"), the Company has carried out a placing of, and subscription for, new Ordinary Shares (the "
Fundraise Shares
" and together with the WRAP Retail Offer Shares, the "
New Ordinary Shares
"). Since the Fundraise Announcement was published, the Company has received additional subscriptions totalling £30,000 for 1,333,333 further Fundraise Shares, and accordingly, the Company has raised an aggregate amount of approximately £2.15 million (before expenses) (the "
Fundraise
") at a price of 2.25 pence per Fundraise Share (the "
Fundraise Price
"). The Fundraise Price represents a discount of approximately 2 per cent. to the mid-market closing price of an Ordinary Share on 16 July 2026 (being the latest practicable date prior to the Fundraise Announcement). The issue price of the WRAP Retail Offer Shares is equal to the Fundraise Price.
A separate announcement has been made regarding the Fundraise and its terms and sets out the reasons for the Fundraise and use of proceeds. The proceeds of the WRAP Retail Offer will be utilised in the same way as the proceeds of the Fundraise.
For the avoidance of doubt, the WRAP Retail Offer is not part of the Fundraise. Completion of the WRAP Retail Offer is conditional, inter alia, upon the completion of the Fundraise but completion of the Fundraise is not conditional on the completion of the WRAP Retail Offer.
The WRAP Retail Offer and the Fundraise are conditional on the New Ordinary Shares being admitted to trading on AIM ("
Admission
"). It is anticipated that Admission will become effective and that dealings in the New Ordinary Shares will commence on AIM at 08.00 a.m. on 31 July 2026 (and not on 28 July 2026 as previously indicated in the Company's announcement on 17 July 2026).
WRAP Retail Offer
The Company values its retail shareholder base and believes that it is appropriate to provide both new and existing retail shareholders in the United Kingdom the opportunity to participate in the WRAP Retail Offer.
Therefore, the Company is making the WRAP Retail Offer open to eligible investors in the United Kingdom, being new or existing shareholders of Bradda Head Lithium, following release of this announcement and through certain financial intermediaries.
A number of retail platforms are able to access the WRAP Retail Offer. Non-holders or existing shareholders wishing to subscribe for Retail Offer Shares should contact their broker or wealth manager who will confirm if they are participating in the Retail Offer.
Retail brokers wishing to participate in the Retail Offer on behalf of eligible retail investors, should contact WRAP@winterflood.com.
The Retail Offer
is expected to close at 4.30 p.m. on 27 July 2026. Eligible retail investors should note that financial intermediaries may have earlier closing times.
The result of the Retail Offer is expected to be announced by the Company on or around
28 July
2026.
To be eligible to participate in the Retail Offer, applicants must be a customer of a participating intermediary including individuals aged 18 years or over, companies and other bodies corporate, partnerships, trusts, associations and other unincorporated organisations.
There is a minimum subscription of £100 per investor under the Retail Offer. The terms and conditions on which investors subscribe will be provided by the relevant financial intermediaries including relevant commission or fee charges.
The Company reserves the right to amend the size and timings of the retail offer at its discretion. The Company reserves the right to scale back any order and to reject any application for subscription under the WRAP Retail Offer without giving any reason for such rejection.
It is vital to note that once an application for Retail Offer Shares has been made and accepted via an intermediary, it cannot be withdrawn.
The Retail Offer Shares will, when issued, be credited as fully paid, and have the right to receive all dividends and other distributions declared, made or paid after their date of issue.
It is a term of the WRAP Retail Offer that the total value of the WRAP Retail Offer Shares available for subscription at the Fundraise Price does not exceed £200,000, or such size as agreed by the Company.
It should be noted that the Warrants do not guarantee any return and will expire if not exercised prior to their expiry date. If the share price of the Company does not exceed the exercise price of the Warrants prior to their expiry date then it is unlikely that any of the Warrants would be exercised.
Investors should make their own investigations into the merits of an investment in the Company. Nothing in this announcement amounts to a recommendation to invest in the Company or amounts to investment, taxation or legal advice.
It should be noted that a subscription for Ordinary Shares and investment in the Company carries a number of risks, including the risk that investors may lose their entire investment. Investors should take independent advice from a person experienced in advising on investment in securities such as the Ordinary Shares if they are in any doubt.
An investment in the Company will place capital at risk. The value of investments, and any income, can go down as well as up, so investors could get back less than the amount invested.

The Retail Offer is not being made into any jurisdiction other than the United Kingdom.

company_30s.what_they_do: Bradda Head Ltd is a junior mining company focused on lithium exploration and development.  Its flagship project is the Whistlejacket lithium deposit in the UK, where the team is drilling for high‑grade resources that could feed the growing battery‑cell market.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Lithium is a key component of electric‑vehicle batteries and renewable‑energy storage.  The UK and Europe are pushing for local supply chains, giving Bradda a strategic advantage.  If Whistlejacket turns out to be a sizeable, low‑cost deposit, it could become a critical supplier for the region’s battery industry.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the exploration phase with no revenue yet.  It has secured a key drilling permit, signed an MOU with an energy partner, and is raising capital through a wrap‑retail offer.  Cash burn is high, but the company is actively moving toward a first‑stage production plan.

rns_narrative: Bradda has been busy raising funds and building partnerships.  The wrap‑retail offer and a new MOU with Tyfast Energy are designed to shore up cash for drilling and development.  Meanwhile, research firms and a defense consortium are taking notice, signalling growing confidence in the project’s potential.

The company’s narrative has shifted from a pure exploration play to a more structured development strategy.  The recent drilling permit and partnership with a defense industrial base suggest a move toward operational milestones.
Overall, the company appears to be stabilising its capital position and positioning Whistlejacket for a future resource report.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet anticipation – investors are watching the next funding round and resource report before committing.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the rising global lithium demand, the company’s strategic partnerships, and the successful securing of a drilling permit as evidence that Whistlejacket could become a valuable asset.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company still has no revenue, is burning cash, and may face regulatory or technical setbacks that could stall the project.  They also note that junior miners often over‑estimate resource quality.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has moved from neutral to cautiously bullish as the company moves from fundraising to active drilling and partnership announcements.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – there is no current public chatter, meaning the market is largely unaware of the upcoming catalysts.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the initial drilling phase at Whistlejacket, with a published resource estimate that meets or exceeds the 2025 guidance.
